articles.title: My longterm boyfriend died last year. Is it too soon to date someone new? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: Only you can know when you are ready, but a year is not long to process grief, and you seem to have doubts about this man. My long term boyfriend died of cancer last year. We’d been together for 16 years, since I was 21 and he was 23.
body: I loved my late partner deeply and had planned to stay with him for ever. We were embarking on an 18-year project together, raising our son. Now I think, how can I ever be happy again?

Before he died, my partner told me to find a single dad to go out with. When I returned to work, a colleague I had considered a flirt was away – getting chemo. Now he’s in remission. He’s also a single parent. Lately, I’ve realised I have a crush on him. His life has been touched by tragedy and he knows what’s important to him. He’s very kind, like my late partner, and I think we click.

What gives me a lot of pause is that I find him to blow hot and cold. Also, because I’m a solo mum I don’t really have time for someone else. But he has recently left the company, so I wouldn’t be dating a co-worker.
I s it remarkable to meet a single dad you genuinely like? Or are there more out there than I think? Please tell me what you think I should do.
points: Only you can know when you are ready, but a year is not long to process grief, and you seem to have doubts about this man.
My long term boyfriend died of cancer last year.
We’d been together for 16 years, since I was 21 and he was 23.
We were embarking on an 18-year project together, raising our son.

articles.title: ‘We hang on to summer a little longer here’: five of the best places for autumn sun in Europe and Turkey
articles.summary: If you’re looking for a last blast of summer, these sunny resorts offer quiet beaches but enough life to stave off the end-of-season blues. A Kalkan sunset is always a beautiful thing – the horseshoe-shaped bay deepening to azure blue against an apricot-rose sky – but, in October, when the light is…
body: For me, the best thing about an autumn break – besides the sunsets – is that I can visit some of my favourite places that just get overrun in summer. The glittering beach at Kaputas, sandwiched into a triangular gap on the mountainous Kalkan-Kas road, has become a victim of Instagram; from May to September, it’s impossible to get near. In October, the waters are still warm and the beach – although still busy – has plenty of space for a dip and a laze.

About 20 minutes’ drive inland, the mountain village of Bezirgan, which used to serve as a summer retreat for wealthier Kalkan residents, settles back into complete peace in autumn, save for the woodpeckers battering away at the bark of the almond trees and the squirrels skittering through the leaves. The Lycian Way weaves through the village, past Ottoman-era grain stores, with the lush gardens of the Pirha Köy Sofrası restaurant a great bet for a plate of traditional manti (dumplings in yoghurt) or kofte (meatballs), before setting off for a hike (they do fantastic breakfasts too).
points: If you’re looking for a last blast of summer, these sunny resorts offer quiet beaches but enough life to stave off the end-of-season blues.

articles.title: Going nowhere fast? Personal trainers on why you aren’t seeing results in the gym
articles.summary: From doing too much cardio to wasting time – PTs reveal the common fails stunting your progress, and how to avoid them. We’ve all done it. Launched ourselves head first into a new regime – perhaps as the result of a new year resolution, recent breakup or aggressively unflattering photo.
body: A better approach is to devise a realistic training schedule that actually aligns with your lifestyle. “When getting started, lower the bar,” she suggests. “Aim for two weekly strength sessions done consistently. If you manage that, and have the time, energy and inclination to do more, you can always add in a third. It’s much easier to build on something you’re doing consistently than repeatedly start over with something that’s unsustainable.”

“There’s an outdated belief that you must ‘keep the body guessing’ in order for it to adapt, by continually switching up your workouts,” says Nick Finney, who has trained Robbie Williams and Jennifer Lopez. “I understand that people want to avoid boredom by changing what they do each workout, but it ends up hindering their progress. You need to practise your technique, become more proficient and give your body time to improve and get stronger. If you keep changing things up, then it’s impossible to measure progress by comparing what you achieved in previous workouts.”
points: From doing too much cardio to wasting time – PTs reveal the common fails stunting your progress, and how to avoid them.

articles.title: How Australia’s tipping culture got awkward – and what to do about it
articles.summary: Ten per cent, 20%, 25%? If you’ve made a cashless payment at a cafe or pub lately there’s a reasonable chance you’ve been prompted to tip. Isabella Lee looks into the arrival of US-style tip requests and where that money really goes.
body: Alyx: You’ve been thinking about tipping for a few months now, and wrote about it this week. What first sparked your interest? Isabella: I came across a post in a bartenders’ Facebook group from someone asking if their experience of having tips withheld was normal. The comments shocked me! There were more than 30 responses, with the majority of them calling out venues where they’d also been denied their tips. It made me think, if this practice was so common, why hadn’t anything been done about it?

Alyx: When you did some more digging, what did you find out? Isabella: I reached out to Fair Work to ask what legislation there was around paying out tips to staff. They told me there is none. So the original poster hadn’t experienced wage theft because the employers weren’t actually breaking any rules. It’s not just management who can dip their hand in the tip jar. Cashless payment systems take a percentage from every transaction made too. It’s pretty cheeky that the systems that allow a business to ask for tips – which changes customers’ decision-making behaviour – also get a cut.
points: If you’ve made a cashless payment at a cafe or pub lately there’s a reasonable chance you’ve been prompted to tip.

articles.title: Exclusive: The Story Behind Hailey Bieber’s Jet-Black Mani at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala
articles.summary: Hailey Bieber attended the sixth Academy Museum Gala with a new nail look: the jet-black mani. Here, Vogue speaks to Bieber’s go-to nail artist Zola Ganzorigt for the exclusive BTS details.
body: Just as one can never go wrong with a little black dress, a glossy black manicure is a classic. Case in point: Hailey Bieber at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala, where she artfully contrasted a bubblegum-pink Chanel column gown by Matthieu Blazy with jet-black nails.

The Rhode founder tapped go-to celebrity nail artist Zola Ganzorigt, an OPI global ambassador, for the bold look. The process was fairly simple: Ganzorigt gave Bieber’s nails an almond shape to elongate her fingers before using the OPI Intelli-Gel in Black Onyx for that moody, glossy black shade—somewhat mirroring the deep, dark chocolate hair that Bieber debuted in September.

Tonight marks the Academy Museum’s sixth annual gala in Los Angeles, where Bieber joins other A-listers—including honorees Colman Domingo and Charlize Theron and special performer Taylor Swift —to celebrate cinema.

articles.title: The Story Behind Emma Chamberlain’s Classic Hollywood Look for the 2026 Academy Museum Gala
articles.summary: “The after-party is at the Chateau. It just feels like, ‘This is LA, baby! This is Hollywood.’ And we’re going to do it exactly like that,” Chamberlain told Vogue ahead of Saturday’s gala event.
body: As a Met Gala regular, Chamberlain knows how to deliver a fan-favorite look. Case in point: This year, she wore a hand-painted custom Mugler gown by Miguel Castro Freitas that turned her body into a canvas.

Tonight, for the 2026 Academy Museum Gala—a fundraiser honoring Charlize Theron, Colman Domingo, and John Carpenter, and featuring a performance by Taylor Swift—Chamberlain took on a different sartorial challenge: going classic Hollywood. For her and her stylist, Jared Ellner, that meant a custom red Giorgio Armani gown and makeup by Armani Beauty.

Newly brunette, Chamberlain drew inspiration from iconic actors like Audrey Hepburn and Winona Ryder when envisioning her look. Ryder, in particular, was something of a dark brunette mascot for Chamberlain. “When I was going from the blonde to the brunette, Winona Ryder was a huge inspo for me,” she said. “I was looking at photos of her constantly, to kind of help me gain the courage to dye it brown.”

articles.title: The Best Dressed Stars From the 2026 Academy Museum Gala
articles.summary: The best dressed stars of the night were those who leaned into classic Hollywood glamour—with a twist.
body: This evening, the 2026 Academy Museum Gala—now in its sixth year running—gathered an A-list crowd to celebrate and advance the museum's mission to “celebrate and preserve cinema.”

Co-chaired by Tom Ford, Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg, and Kate Capshaw, the special evening naturally brought together an impressive list of Hollywood heavyweights—including the special honorees of the night, which included Charlize Theron, the recipient of the Icon Award; Luminary Award winner John Carpenter; and Colman Domingo, who took home the Vantage Award. Oh, and Taylor Swift was also in the house, delivering a special performance.

Highlights included actor Naomi Ackie, who kicked off the red carpet in a fabulous purple Balenciaga strapless gown—complete with a tiered, voluminous silhouette. Other stars went more sleek and streamlined, like Maya Hawke in her crystal bejeweled Prada column gown, or Mia Goth in her slinky black sequin Dior dress.

Whether it was the night’s special honorees, including Charlize Theron and Colman Domingo, or the actors simply out for some glamorous fun, the red carpet was filled with stellar sightings. Among them? Taylor Swift, who is due to perform at the gala later this evening.

Before heading inside to the main stage, Swift hit the step-and-repeat in custom Dior by Jonathan Anderson with Chopard jewelry. The star opted for classic Hollywood glitz, choosing a strapless, icy-blue gown that featured delicate pleating and a laced-up detail at the front. She accessorized with a pair of platinum earrings set with 32.40 carats of diamonds, a gold ring set with 5.78 carats of diamonds, and a platinum and diamond bracelet, all from Chopard’s haute joaillerie collection. A loosely curled lob and a light pink lip completed the look.

articles.title: Île Seguin: This tiny island just outside Paris is about to become the city's newest cultural destination
articles.summary: A sleek new contemporary art center is opening on Île Seguin this October, marking another milestone in the transformation of this former industrial site on the Seine.
body: Paris is hardly short of museums and is a real paradise for art lovers. Not only could you spend weeks hopping between its biggest hitters—namely the Louvre, Musée d'Orsay, and Musée de l'Orangerie —but the city also has an incredible collection of smaller museums and galleries that are less frequented by tourists, yet definitely deserve some love. If, like me, you have a particular soft spot for contemporary art, Gagosian and Perrotin are just two of the many galleries worth visiting in the city, and they're among my favorites to browse on a rainy Parisian day.

Although the city center has countless museums to visit, this autumn, one of the French capital's most exciting cultural openings is happening somewhere you might not immediately think to look: on a small island in the Seine just beyond the city limits.

Île Seguin sits at Boulogne-Billancourt, southwest of central Paris and around a 10-minute walk from the end of Métro line 9. Once synonymous with industry—Renault operated its enormous factory here for much of the 20th century—the island has been gradually reinventing itself as a cultural district. Now, the next major piece of the puzzle is about to be added.
